title: 5 reasons why you SHOULDN'T jump on TRT
summary: NH gives five reasons young lifters should not start TRT: their low testosterone is usually lifestyle-caused, TRT ties gains to drugs and invites escalation, it shuts down natural production, exogenous hormones are not healthy and mask root causes, and it is a lifelong dependency. He urges fixing lifestyle and training naturally for years first.
claims: TRT became the new YouTube fitness fraud once open PED promotion ran its course
TRT is meant to be a replacement, which presupposes something missing; you can't replace what is there or can be there
Youth clinics expanding their business are spreading TRT to very young men, a catastrophic trend
Fantasizing about when your testosterone will crash in 10-20 years, while it works fine now, is a toxic slippery-slope mindset
For about 99% of people claiming low T, there is no genetic condition; it comes from environment and lifestyle
Many claim low T without blood tests, just because they're small, when they simply haven't trained
Video games, junk food, alcohol and no physical activity give the body no reason to produce testosterone
People 60 years ago weren't commonly low T; the generational difference is environmental, not genetic
Fix diet, quit video games, get sun and train 3-4 years before getting tested again; only then discuss solutions
Being skinnier at 17 is normal; you'll grow with time
TRT clinics are not impartial; they want to sell hormones and will prescribe to almost anyone who pays
TRT gives fast results that come from the drug, not training, robbing you of making your first gains through training
Having felt TRT's effect, people tend to escalate doses, even sourcing drugs themselves; few stick to one cycle or small doses
TRT shuts down natural production, and the longer you stay on, the harder it is to restart
Someone who started with low T and comes off TRT may end up with near-zero testosterone, risking severe depression and self-harm
Even three years of slow gains at 16-17 to kickstart your hormones is worth it over a lifelong chemical crutch
NH started training skinny-fat with a gamer, junk food, low-water, low-sleep lifestyle and made very small gains for a long time
Never settle on a permanent resolution to fix a temporary problem
Some people spend a full year trying to restart their hormonal profile after TRT without success
NH weighs about 100 lb more than as a teen; his friends who didn't change their environment stayed the same
Without training he would be 26, six feet and about 160 lb
Even at normal-range doses, exogenous testosterone causes damage because it can't replicate natural production
TRT masks a toxic lifestyle like a painkiller on an unhealed wound; fixing the lifestyle fixes both health and testosterone
TRT is for life: losing money, insurance coverage or legal access, or travelling to countries that ban it, all become serious problems
Gains from a vial rob you of the pride of having transformed yourself
NH had all the signs of low T when young (low energy, almost no gains) and stuck with training until rewarded
Naturals build their physique by keeping the body in its own anabolic environment for a long time; stability lets muscle grow
Influencers who used PEDs for years and crashed their hormones call it TRT, but they are replacing nothing; it's still drugs
